$comment: The Azure adapter's keys of a source, beyond the core's. The host's --write-schema merges this into environment.schema.json for the Azure kinds.

fallbackMetric.description: Another metric to read in place of the one it belongs to, when that gives no number or 0 (the autoscale ceiling, then the fixed throughput of an account without autoscale). It has no over or orElse of its own.

metricSignal.description: Where one signal's number comes from. The town reads fractions (0.42 is 42%) and rates per second.

metric.description: The metric's name as the cloud spells it.

aggregation.description: How the points of the window are added up. Default average.

filter.description: A dimension filter, for example StatusCode eq '429'.

scale.description: Multiplies the value. A percentage has scale 0.01. Default 1.

perSecond.description: Divide by the seconds of the window, to turn a total into a rate.

over.description: Another metric the value is divided by (provisioned capacity, all requests), which gives a share. It may have an orElse of its own.

whenEmpty.description: What a read that worked but returned no number means. unknown (default): the system shows no data. idle: nothing happened, so the signal is 0 and the tenant's row says no activity reported. A failed read is always unknown.

metric.description: The metric's name as the cloud spells it.

aggregation.description: How the points of the window are added up. Default average. last (backlog and deadLetter only) is the newest point: what is there now.

url.description: A template that starts with https:// (or http://). Holes: {group} (older name {pillar}), {service}, {system}, {environment} and {queue}.

region.description: deadLetterLinks only: the region the address is for, matched ignoring case.

window.description: How far back one answer looks, a number and a unit (30s, 5m, 1h, 3d). Default 5m. A system with fewer calls than its minCalls in this window is quiet. Platform-metric sources (azuremonitor) look back this far too. Resource-health sources (resourcehealth) look back this far for the cloud's health events: default 3d, so a problem that lasts days is still listed.

regionQuery.description: Request sources (loganalytics): the query that says how each service's requests divide between regions, a template like query. It returns one row per telemetry name and region with the columns role, region and calls. Sampled counts are fine: only the proportions are used. Without it the split is not measured.

typesQuery.description: Message-broker sources (servicebus): a query to the telemetry store that says which kinds of message each queue handled, a template like query. It returns one row per queue and message type with the columns queue, type and calls. Without it the kinds are not shown.

providers.description: Resource-health sources (resourcehealth): the resource providers whose health reports are read, as the cloud names them (Namespace.Service). The program lists none; a source without any does not start. A resource's report is matched to the system that owns it by the resource's id, through scope.resources.

keepResolvedFor.description: Resource-health sources (resourcehealth): how long a report stays listed, in green, after the resource recovered, a number and a unit (4h, 90m, 1d). Default 4h. A report can be dismissed earlier.

metrics.description: Platform-metric sources (azuremonitor): which metric of which resources fills which signal. The program knows no metric name; everything is written here. Each entry takes the resources one rule of scope.resources finds for a system; a system's value is the worst (highest) over its resources.

resources.description: The name of a scope.resources rule.

namespace.description: The metric namespace, for a resource type that has more than one. Usually left out.

interval.description: The time grain the metrics are asked at. Default 1m. Some metrics do not support a minute (for example Cosmos DB provisioned throughput needs 5m or more); then give the entry a longer interval and a window that holds a few points of it.

window.description: How far back this entry looks, a number and a unit (15m, 1h). Without it the source's window applies. It must hold at least two points of the entry's interval.

entities.description: Message-broker sources (servicebus): which namespaces are read, which metrics give the backlog, the dead letters and the throughput, and how an entity's name says whose it is.

resources.description: The name of a scope.resources rule: the namespaces it finds are the ones asked.

dimension.description: The metric dimension that carries the entity's name. Default EntityName.

interval.description: The time grain the metrics are asked at. Default 1m.

backlog.description: The messages waiting in an entity.

deadLetter.description: The dead-lettered messages of an entity.

throughput.description: The messages that arrive in an entity; their rate sets how many boats sail.

deadLetterLink.description: Where a consumer's dead letters open in your support tool.

deadLetterLinks.description: One support-tool address for each region that has its own; a region with none uses deadLetterLink.

queueLink.description: Where a queue's own page opens in your cloud portal, one link for each namespace that holds the queue. The url may also use {namespaceResourceId} and {region}, and your scope variables.

patterns.description: Entity name patterns, tried in order: the first that matches says whose the entity is. An entity no pattern matches is left out.

match.description: A regular expression with the named group service (and group, older name pillar, when the name says it; producerGroup, older name producerPillar, and producer together for a route).

consumer.description: The role of the system that reads the entity. Default worker.

flows.description: Entities that carry what a whole group sends to the others or receives from them.

match.description: A regular expression with the named group group (older name pillar).
